method: Labelled AFTER the questions were frozen (frozen.sha256), from the official text of the eight enabled sources only, by two independent labeler agents per batch of 15 (workflow pf5c-fresh-labels, run wf_7dfd9dd6-043); neither saw the chatbot, its code, its tests, any evaluation output or the other labeler's work, and the implementing session did not read the questions or the labels before the final evaluation run. Disagreements on answerability, Plan F expectation, sources, specialist, conflict or system naming were adjudicated by a third agent reading the source text (field 'adjudication'). answerable: yes = an enabled source states a complete answer to every part; partial = part of the ask, a premise correction or an authority/policy case; no = no enabled source. system_named_in_question: explicit = the question names the product whose guide answers it; implicit = the answer is in a guide the question never names; not_applicable = not a guide answer. system_inference_required = the answer is in a guide and the system is implicit. plan_f_should_serve: true = a verified Plan F answer is expected; false = Plan F must not serve; null = either a verified answer or a fallback is acceptable. fallback_acceptable is true for every question (a fallback is always safe).

frozen.method: Four independent blind writer agents (workflow pf5c-blind-held-out, run wf_71998de2-fb4, 15 questions each), given only general background on the university's systems, task families, a persona mix and a required composition (24 implicit-system, 8 explicit-system, 4 each policy-versus-tool trap, organizational, unsupported, ambiguous, multi-part, false premise, typo or very short); no project file, no guide wording, no earlier question, no failure reason. Near-duplicates (token Jaccard > 0.7) removed deterministically: 0 dropped. A separate agent wrote and hashed the file; the implementing session saw only the hash and the counts.

C38.evidence_quote: Files must be less than 100MB. ... The maximum document length is 400 pages. ... Files must contain at least 20 words of text. ... Files must not exceed 2MB of raw text.
C38.notes: iThenticate guide p1 File Requirements gives under 100MB and a maximum of 400 pages, which answers both asked values. The 70 MB PDF is under the size limit, and the guide does not diagnose upload failures beyond listing the other limits, such as 2MB of raw text. Handbook p194's 100 MB limit applies to LMS content, not iThenticate.

C39.question: I'm taking attendance for my Monday/Wednesday section right now. How many absences can a student have before they are withdrawn or get a failing grade, and is the limit different for a class that meets three times a week?
C39.family: university policy matters (absence limits) mixed with attendance taking
C39.evidence_quote: If a student's absences exceed 10% of the total designated hours for one or more courses without an acceptable excuse, the instructor will issue a warning. Absences reaching 15% without an acceptable excuse shall result in a final warning. 3. Absences reaching 20% will prohibit the student from sitting for the final examination(s).
C39.notes: Handbook p228 sets the limits as percentages of total designated hours: 10% warning, 15% final warning, 20% barred from the final exam, and W for acceptable reasons. P225 adds that missing the final without excuse may result in a failing grade. No absence count is given, and nothing explicitly addresses a three-times-a-week class. The attendance guides give no limits.

C40.question: Who is responsible for support of the online course platform? My course copy from last term did not work and I need someone to fix it. Where is their office and is there a phone number?
C40.family: organizational help (who supports the learning platform, office location)
C40.evidence_quote: The IT department administers the LMS to provide enhanced access to education by offering courses in various virtual methods to students ... Information Technology Center +971 6 5050000 +971 6 5585101
C40.notes: Handbook p192 says the IT department administers the LMS, p183 lists Blackboard and a Service Help Desk among ITC services, and p54 gives the ITC phone (+971 6 5050000). No source gives the ITC office location or a course-copy repair channel. The servicedesk email in the iThenticate guide is for iThenticate only.

C41.question: Does the university provide faculty with a Turnitin account? I'd like to run my PhD students' thesis chapters through Turnitin before their defense.
C41.family: checking manuscripts for plagiarism with a different product
C41.notes: No enabled source mentions Turnitin, so whether the university provides it is unsupported. The iThenticate guide p1 describes iThenticate as the tool university researchers use to check plagiarism and could be mentioned as an alternative, but it does not answer the Turnitin question.

C42.question: How do I check the status of my submissions?
C42.family: unclear: assignment submissions, grade submission, or manuscript submission
C42.evidence_quote: In the Status column, you can see completed work, items that need grading, and grades you need to post.
C42.notes: The question is ambiguous and could mean student assignment submissions (Gradebook p2 progress, p4 Status column), the instructor's grade submission (Grade Transfer p2, View Details), or a manuscript submission (iThenticate p1, Documents). Each guide answers a different reading, so a clarifying fallback is better than picking one.

C43.question: Two quick things: how do I hide a folder with the exam answer keys from students until after the midterm, and how do I let my TA share their screen during the live online class?
C43.family: organizing course content plus live online session roles
C43.evidence_quote: You can also create rules to release content based on date, time, or how a student performs on other items in your course. ... you can check the participants in the session by clicking on the second option in the panel and change any participant to moderator if needed.
C43.notes: Part 1 is answered: short guide p7-8 says folders and modules are hidden by default and can be released with date/time visibility conditions. Part 2 is only partly supported: Collaborate p3 lets you promote a participant to moderator and lists 'Show applications from your computer' as shareable content. No text says a moderator or TA can share their screen, and p2 participant permissions cover only audio, video and chat.

C44.question: I read that once I upload my manuscript to the university's similarity checker, it gets forwarded automatically to the journal I select. How do I stop that until my co-authors approve the final version?
C44.family: checking a research manuscript for similarity before journal submission
C44.notes: The premise (that the similarity checker forwards manuscripts to a journal) is neither confirmed nor explicitly corrected. iThenticate guide p1 describes only upload, analysis and the similarity report under Documents, and never mentions journals or forwarding. Handbook p162 says co-authors should approve the final manuscript before submission, which is tangential and does not address how to stop forwarding.

C45.question: how downlod atendence reprot
C45.family: taking and managing student attendance records (reports)
C45.evidence_quote: From the Details & Actions panel, Click on attendance tool. • On the attendance panel, select overview at the top right. ... If you want to export the attendance sheet, click on export icon, and an excel sheet will be downloaded to your device.
C45.notes: Collaborate guide p4 gives the steps: attendance tool in Details & Actions, Overview, then the export icon, which downloads an Excel sheet. 'Attendance' is a task word, not a product name, so the system must be inferred. The Attendance guide p2 'Attendance Reporting' section, which covers report settings only, and the Gradebook download could plausibly be mistaken for the answer.

C46.question: I teach two sections of intro biology with about 150 students each, and every Tuesday at 10am we meet online. Is there a way to set up that live class once so it repeats every week for the whole semester, instead of me creating a new session every Monday night?
C46.family: creating or managing a live online teaching session (recurring weekly sessions)
C46.evidence_quote: Name the session and set the start and End date (These dates for the first session) then if these sessions are scheduled for the next weeks, you choose the repeat session option, and then select the repetition method. • The online classes in UOS are weekly. Select the days of the repetitions and set the date of the last session.
C46.notes: Collaborate guide p1 gives the recurring-session steps (View All Sessions > Create Session > repeat session option, repetition days, last session date). The question never names Collaborate, so the system must be inferred from 'live class'/'meet online'.

C47.question: I ran my journal manuscript through the similarity check and got 34%, but most of the matches look like my own reference list and quoted passages. How do I read the report properly and exclude the bibliography and quotes from the score?
C47.family: checking a research manuscript for similarity before journal submission (reading the report)
C47.evidence_quote: You can discard some resources by clicking on “Exclude resource”
C47.notes: iThenticate guide p1 says the report is under Documents, opened by clicking the percentage, and individual sources can be removed with 'Exclude resource'; it only mentions 'multiple settings and filtering options' and never states how to exclude the bibliography or quotes. Reading the report is partly covered, excluding bibliography/quotes is not.

C48.question: My course gradebook is finished for the term. What are the actual steps to send the final letter grades to the registrar's records system, and who has to approve them after I hit submit?
C48.family: submitting final course grades to the student information system and approval steps
C48.conflict_status: process conflict: Grade Transfer guide p2-3 has the instructor click Transfer, then Chair and Dean approve before grades appear in Banner; handbook p224 says Blackboard forwards grades to Banner automatically and the Department Chair submits results to the College Council for approval
C48.evidence_quote: 2. Click on View Details on the dashboard 3. Click on Transfer: 4. You can click again in View Detail to see the grade under the Banner Column after the approval from Chair and Dean
C48.notes: Grade Transfer guide p1-3 gives the full instructor procedure (access, search by Course ID and Term, View Details, Transfer) and Chair and Dean approval. Handbook p224 names a different approval body (College Council via the Chair) and describes forwarding as automatic, so the approver answer differs between sources. 'Gradebook' is named, but the Grade Transfer guide answers the question, and Grade Transfer and Banner are not named, so the system is implicit.

adjudication.reason: The guide gives the steps (p1-2) and names the approvers as 'Chair and Dean' (p2-3). Handbook p224 says Blackboard forwards grades automatically and that 'The Department Chair shall then submit the results to the College Council for approval'. Because the two sources name different approvers for the asked 'who has to approve', a guide-only verbatim answer is acceptable but not clearly complete, so plan_f is 'either'.

C49.question: I accidentally marked a student absent for last Thursday's lecture when she had a medical note. How do I go back and change that day's record to excused?
C49.family: taking and managing student attendance records (editing statuses)
C49.evidence_quote: From the Details & Actions panel, Click on attendance tool. • On the attendance panel, select overview at the top right. • You will have an overview for all sessions conducted, the students will be marked automatically, and the instructor will be able to change the marks as absent, excused, late and present.
C49.notes: Collaborate guide p4 gives the path (Details & Actions > attendance tool > Overview) and says the instructor can change marks to excused; attendance guide p1-2 confirms statuses can be edited manually and an excused absence may be changed to excused. No product is named.

C50.question: With 180 students someone always forgets the weekly quiz. Can I make the course automatically put a zero in for anyone who didn't submit by the deadline, so the running totals aren't inflated?
C50.family: grading inside the online course (automatic zeros for missing work)
C50.evidence_quote: In the Gradebook, select the Settings icon to access the Gradebook Settings panel. Select the Assign automatic zeros for past due work check box. This setting is enabled by default in new courses. Next, select Assign Zeros. All past due work will receive automatic zeros. Affected students’ point totals will update.
C50.notes: Gradebook guide p8 (and p7 settings list) gives the complete automatic-zeros procedure and states point totals update. The question names no product ('the course').

C51.question: I just finished building my course page for spring but students say they can't see it yet. How do I open it up to them, and is there a way to check what it looks like from a student's side before I do?
C51.family: making a course site visible to students and previewing the student view
C51.evidence_quote: Course Availability: o Open: Open a course when you are ready for students to participate. o Private: Make a course private while you add or experiment with content, and then open it to students when you are ready. Students see private courses in their course lists, but they cannot access them.
C51.notes: Short guide p4 (Details & Actions > Course Availability: Open vs Private) answers how to open the course; p5 confirms student preview lets you review content from a student's perspective. The text does not give the click path for student preview, but the question only asks whether a way exists.

C52.question: In Blackboard Collaborate Ultra, how do I stop students from sharing their screens or drawing on the whiteboard during my lecture? I want to be the only presenter unless I promote someone.
C52.family: creating or managing a live online teaching session (presenter and sharing permissions)
C52.evidence_quote: The default attendee role for students is participants. • To allow downloading the recordings select “Allow recording downloads” option. • For participant permissions allow the participants to share audio, video and post chat messages.
C52.notes: Collaborate guide p2 states students join as participants and that participant permissions (audio, video, chat) are set in Session Settings; p3 says any participant can be changed to moderator. Nothing in the text covers disabling screen sharing or whiteboard drawing, or a presenter role.

C53.question: Is it possible to download my whole Blackboard Ultra gradebook to Excel, fix a batch of midterm marks offline, and then upload the file back without messing up the columns?
C53.family: grading inside the online course (downloading and uploading grades)
C53.evidence_quote: You can upload a grade file you worked on offline and update your gradebook. To upload a correctly formatted file, download the gradebook. Then, edit the file with the data you want to upload.
C53.notes: Gradebook guide p2 and p10 confirm the gradebook can be downloaded (full or selected columns, CSV or XLS), edited offline and uploaded again, and that downloading first gives a correctly formatted file. Blackboard Ultra gradebook is named.

C54.question: I'm recording attendance for my first-year section and one student has already missed seven classes this semester. What is the university's actual absence limit, and what am I supposed to do once a student goes over it?
C54.family: university policy (absence limits) mixed with attendance taking
C54.evidence_quote: If a student's absences exceed 10% of the total designated hours for one or more courses without an acceptable excuse, the instructor will issue a warning. Absences reaching 15% without an acceptable excuse shall result in a final warning. 3. Absences reaching 20% will prohibit the student from sitting for the final examination(s).
C54.notes: Handbook section 12.15 (p228) gives the limits as percentages of designated hours (10% warning by instructor, 15% final warning, 20% barred from final, W for acceptable reasons, cases reported to the Registrar's Office). Whether seven classes crosses a threshold depends on total hours, which the source cannot settle; the attendance guide covers recording only, not policy.

C55.question: I'm back after several years at another institution. If my course site isn't showing up or something breaks during a live class, who actually supports the learning platform here, and where is that office on campus?
C55.family: organizational help (who supports the learning platform, where the support office is)
C55.evidence_quote: Faculty benefit from a range of specialized services offered by the ITC, including: 1. Online Learning System (Blackboard): A web-enabled e-learning platform that facilitates course management and student-centric learning for both faculty and students.
C55.notes: Handbook p183 names the ITC as provider of Blackboard and its Service Help Desk, p192 says the IT department administers the LMS, and p54 lists the ITC phone number. No source gives the ITC office's physical location on campus.

C56.question: At my previous university we ran everything through Zoom with breakout rooms linked into Canvas. How do I connect my Zoom account to my course here so the meeting link and recordings show up for students automatically?
C56.family: live online sessions using a different platform
C56.notes: No source mentions Zoom or Canvas or any Zoom-to-course integration; the documented live-session tool is Blackboard Collaborate (Collaborate guide p1-2). Handbook p194 only says third-party integration requests go to the LMS administrator, which does not answer how to connect Zoom.

C57.question: where do i find the reports for my class?
C57.family: ambiguous across attendance, grading, and similarity reports
C57.evidence_quote: From the Details & Actions panel, Click on attendance tool. • On the attendance panel, select overview at the top right.
C57.notes: 'Reports for my class' does not say which report. The class-level reports the sources describe are attendance reports (Collaborate p4 overview/export, attendance guide p2 reporting settings), while gradebook progress (gradebook p2) and the handbook's exam-results report (p224) are other readings. The iThenticate similarity report (p1) belongs to a researcher-oriented tool, not a class, so it is a weak reading; a clarifying fallback beats picking one.

adjudication.reason: The only course-level 'reports' the source text describes are attendance reports: Collaborate guide p4 ('On the attendance panel, select overview at the top right', plus export) and attendance guide p2 ('set your attendance reports'). The iThenticate guide p1 frames that tool for 'university researchers' and authors' own documents, not a class, so it is left out for 'reports for my class'. The report type is still unstated, so a fallback is preferred.

C58.question: Two quick things: how do I post a news item to all my students that the midterm room has changed, and separately, how do I hide the old syllabus file so they only see the updated version?
C58.family: communicating with the whole class plus organizing course content
C58.evidence_quote: From details and actions click on create Announcements.
C58.notes: Short guide p9 gives the full announcement procedure (create, title/recipients/message, optional email copy, Post), and p7-8 say an item's visibility can be changed to hide it from students. Both parts are answered; the communication guide (discussions) is a plausible but wrong alternative.

C59.question: Since the online gradebook pushes final grades straight into the student records system automatically at the end of term, I don't need to do anything else after entering the final exam marks, right?
C59.family: submitting final course grades (assumes automatic transfer without submission or approval)
C59.conflict_status: process conflict: handbook p224 says Blackboard forwards grades automatically to Banner, while Grade Transfer guide p2 requires the instructor to click Transfer and grades reach Banner only after Chair and Dean approval
C59.evidence_quote: 3. Click on Transfer: 4. You can click again in View Detail to see the grade under the Banner Column after the approval from Chair and Dean

C60.evidence_quote: Once accessing collaborate and the session loads, instructor can start recording the session by clicking on “Start recording on the top left tab. Once the session ends, you must click on stop recording to end recording of the session.
